subject: economics
title: Factory Floor Foundations
welcome_lead: Step onto a factory floor where land, labour, capital and enterprise combine. Discover how stuff actually gets made.
meta_desc: GCSE Economics adventure on production and productivity: factors of production, division of labour and basics.
final_note: Production basics nailed. Time to crunch productivity numbers!

concepts.def: Machines, tools, buildings used to produce.
Risk-taking entrepreneurs who organise the rest.

walkthroughs.body_html: To make anything, firms combine land (fields, oil, water), labour (workers' time/skills), capital (factories, machinery) and enterprise (the entrepreneur who organises and takes risk). Each factor is paid: rent, wages, interest, profit.

Smith (1776) showed 10 workers each doing one step could make 48,000 pins per day vs 200 if each made whole pins alone. Specialisation builds skill, saves time and exploits worker strengths. Downside: boredom, dependency on one task.

Productivity = output per worker per hour. Higher productivity = lower unit costs = competitive prices = better wages and profits. UK productivity lags G7 average — boosting it is a major policy goal.

mcqs.q: Which is an example of CAPITAL?

options: Tasks are split among specialised workers

mcqs.q: How is economic growth shown on a Production Possibility Curve?
options: By an outward shift of the entire curve — reflecting an increase in productive capacity through more or better resources, technology, or skills.
Supply shifts only when consumers want more.
Growth is shown by moving from inside the curve to a point on the curve.
Growth is shown by the curve becoming straighter.

mcqs.q: What causes the supply curve to shift?
options: Supply shifts only when consumers want more.
Changes in production costs, technology, taxes/subsidies, number of producers, expectations — anything affecting supply other than the good's own price.
When demand rises, the supply curve shifts right to meet it.
Money is only valuable if backed by gold.

mcqs.q: What are the functions of money?
options: Growth is shown by the curve becoming straighter.
Money is only valuable if backed by gold.
Money is valuable because it is made of valuable materials.
Medium of exchange, store of value, unit of account, and standard of deferred payment — money must perform these to function as money.
